text.p: Gloucestershire, among the early pace-setters in the English county championship, face an inquest into the state of the pitch being used in their current game with Middlesex.
In one and a half days, 25 wickets have fallen and several batsman have been hit by sharply-rising deliveries. Gloucestershire's Monte Lynch has suffered more than most, having to retire hurt twice.
The pitch will be examined on Friday by a delegation from Lord's, after being reported on the first day by umpires Ray Julian and Peter Willey.
Groundsman David Bridle admitted: "This was the first time we have used it for a championship match although the second eleven played on it once last year. The bounce was certainly very variable."
Gloucestershire, replying to Middlesex's 237, were bowled out for just 99, but reduced the visiting side to 78 for six after rain washed out the morning session.
